groups.//: === LOVE-SONG CLAUSES (templates songTitle._loveClauses) — the period's commonest title shape is a pronoun clause ('I Can't Stop Loving You', 'Will You Love Me Tomorrow', 'Don't Make Me Over', 'Tell Me (You're Coming Back)'). Built from four independent slots (head x verb x object x tail) so the space is thousands, not the few dozen a single-slot 'I %verb% You' frame gives before world uniqueness spends it. Own parts of speech (clHead/clVerb/clTail/clLead) so these phrasal verbs never reach the grammar or the older verb filters. Verb classes: clWarm (wanting, holding), clMine (I-subject only: 'my'), clAche (missing, longing), clPart (leaving, hurting), clOver (what I cannot do: get over, live without), clTouch (takes Tight/Tender). ===
Heads: subject + auxiliary. Each class pairs with the verb classes that read naturally after it.
